subject.title: fix(embeddings): bound openai-compatible requests without AbortSignal

question: Should unsignaled OpenAI-compatible embedding batches preserve the adapter’s existing 10-minute inline budget, or intentionally fail at the new 120-second provider floor?
rationale: Both values govern the same provider surface and imply materially different behavior for existing gateway, CLI, direct-provider, and self-hosted deployments; code review cannot safely choose the permanent latency policy.

options.title: Preserve the 10-minute batch contract
options.body: Keep the transport hang fix but align the unsignaled batch timeout with the existing inline batch budget and retain a separately justified query cap.

options.title: Standardize on 120 seconds
options.body: Adopt the shorter batch deadline with explicit owner approval plus upgrade documentation and proof for slow self-hosted endpoints.

options.title: Move deadlines to entry points
options.body: Require gateway, CLI, and other callers to install operation-specific AbortSignals rather than setting provider-wide implicit deadlines.

recommendation.title: Preserve the 10-minute batch contract
recommendation.body: Keep the transport hang fix but align the unsignaled batch timeout with the existing inline batch budget and retain a separately justified query cap.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work on remote embedding endpoint behavior provides the strongest available current-history routing signal for this cross-caller runtime decision.
